title: Allotropes of carbon
examples: What is the main difference in bonding between diamond and graphite?
Can you explain how graphene is related to graphite?
What makes fullerenes unique compared to the others?

explain.say: Today we are learning about allotropes of carbon.

items: Allotropes are different forms of one element.
Carbon is an element found everywhere.
It can exist in several structural forms.

explain.say: Diamond has a very strong tetrahedral structure.
Graphite has arranged carbon atoms in flat layers.
Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms.
Fullerenes are closed cage-like structures of carbon.
In real life, pencil 'lead' is actually graphite.

faq.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
faq.a: Graphite has delocalised electrons in its layers that can move freely. Diamond has all its electrons strongly bonded in place, so they cannot move.
asks: What makes graphite a good conductor?
Does the bonding in diamond stop electricity flow?

faq.q: Are graphene and graphite the same thing?
faq.a: No, graphene is just one single layer taken from the bulk material of graphite.
asks: Is graphene just a thin sheet of graphite?
What is the relationship between the two materials?

faq.q: How are fullerenes different from the others?
faq.a: Fullerenes have a distinct, closed, cage-like structure, unlike the flat sheets of graphene or the bulk layers of graphite.
asks: What is the shape of a fullerene molecule?

faq.q: Is carbon the only element that forms these allotropes?
faq.a: These specific allotropes are unique to carbon's bonding capabilities. Other elements form different types of compounds.
asks: Can other elements make cage structures?
Is this only possible with carbon?

faq.q: What determines the properties of the allotrope?
faq.a: The way the atoms are arranged and bonded determines the material's physical properties, like hardness or conductivity.
asks: Why is bonding so important here?

facts: Diamond is an allotrope where every carbon atom is bonded to four others.
Graphite consists of layers of carbon atoms arranged in hexagonal rings.
Graphene is a single atomic layer of carbon atoms in a honeycomb lattice.
Fullerenes have a closed, hollow, cage-like structure, like a soccer ball.

quiz.say: Which allotrope has a structure similar to a sheet of honeycomb?
quiz.why: Graphene is defined by its single, two-dimensional sheet of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb pattern.

wrong.0: Diamond has a 3D tetrahedral structure, not a flat sheet.
wrong.1: Graphite has layers, but graphene refers to the single, perfect sheet.
wrong.2: Fullerenes are closed, cage-like shapes, not flat sheets.

quiz.say: Which allotrope is known for its extreme hardness?
quiz.why: Diamond's strong, uniform tetrahedral bonding in three dimensions makes it extremely hard.

wrong.1: Graphite is soft because the layers slide easily over each other.
wrong.2: While very strong, diamond's complete 3D bonding gives it superior bulk hardness.
wrong.3: Their structure is more complex and less universally hard than diamond.

quiz.say: If you were to peel one layer off graphite, what would you get?
quiz.why: Graphite is composed of stacked layers, and removing one layer yields graphene.

wrong.0: The process of peeling one layer specifically results in graphene.
wrong.2: Diamond is a solid crystal structure and cannot be peeled in layers.
wrong.3: Fullerenes are distinct, self-contained cage molecules.
